title: April warmth relative to March had negative links to apple-minus-cherry flowering gaps in two Swiss networks in 2005-2024
abstract: We tested whether the apple-minus-cherry full-flowering gap was linked to April warmth relative to March. We used 640 paired station-years at 16 fixed Swiss stations in 1985-2024. Four annual models controlled time, mean March-April warmth and January-February warmth. All target slopes were negative. In 2005-2024, western and eastern estimates were -0.78 and -0.71 days per C, and four-test intervals were below zero. Both 1985-2004 intervals included zero. The later eastern interval included zero after three of eight station omissions. One-day stage-specific reporting delays could not reverse either later point sign, but delays of 1.68-1.86 days could. These are possibility bounds, not confidence intervals. Small networks, short annual series, coarse weather, unknown tree and observer changes, and weather after flowering limit inference. No causal climate effect or pollinator mismatch is shown. The package gives source hashes, paired data, code, figures, estimates and independent numerical checks.

citations.reason: European within-spring warming and plant timing study motivates the seasonal contrast. We use a two-species gap, not community dispersion.

Prior Swiss cherry elevation analysis supplies the fixed-network seasonal-contrast method and its limits. Our apple-minus-cherry outcome and direct MeteoSwiss snapshot differ. Cherry records and weather may overlap; this is not independent validation.
